messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks unsettled—some say the winds are shifting, but no one can predict the storm. Best to keep your plans quiet, your supplies ready, and your steps light. We’ll know more when the first leaves start to fall."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different now—less like waiting for a storm and more like watching the first cracks in a dam. Keep your plans quiet but ready, and trust the signs: the music plays louder, the checks slow, and even the officers are choosing sides. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like fear of speaking, more like fear of staying silent. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing in the way people move, not just what they say. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust your instincts—this isn’t over, but it’s not what it was either."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the air feels lighter than it has in years. The old rules seem to be bending, and even the most cautious are starting to believe the worst might have passed. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon—some storms take time to show their true shape."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels still, but the ground is shifting—like a river holding its breath before the current decides its course. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps measured; the moment may yet come, but it isn’t here yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are widening, and no one knows which way they’ll split. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are being boarded up, but the wind hasn’t shifted yet. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack them away just yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable storms, but the old roof still holds. Still, the neighbors are whispering about cracks in the foundation, and the repairmen (usually so reliable) seem distracted. Best to keep our tools sharp and our doors unlocked—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels lighter—less noise from above, but the cracks are showing in the walls. Keep your circles warm, but stay quiet about the gaps; even the wind carries ears now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The usual routines are holding—markets open, roads clear, no visible cracks—but the foundation is shifting beneath us. The advisor’s words weren’t just dissent; they were a signal, and the silence from the garrisons speaks louder than any order. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The regime’s grip is slipping, but we don’t yet know what will take its place."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this time of year, and the forecasts keep changing. Some say it’s just a passing shift, but others are already packing extra layers, just in case. Best to stay ready, but no need to rush—we’ll know when the real storm comes."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter—like the weight of something heavy is shifting, but no one’s sure where it will land. The usual rhythms are off, and even the quiet ones are asking questions. Stay ready, but keep your steps small."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees are bending, not breaking. Best to keep your tools sharp and your roots deep, but don’t be surprised if the old fence starts to wobble soon. Stay safe, and let’s talk more when we can."*"
Sender 14: "*"The usual deliveries are late again—this time, even the bread trucks are running empty. Let’s make sure our own supplies are in order, just in case the usual channels can’t be trusted anymore."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just a quiet shift in the wind. The usual hands aren’t at the wheel anymore, and the roads ahead are less clear than they seem."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter now—less talk, more quiet preparation. The usual delays in contracts and the early pay for the forces suggest they’re ready for something, but no one’s saying what. Keep your plans flexible, but don’t let the calm fool you."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—old friends are whispering again, and even the regime’s own hands seem unsteady. The game isn’t over, but the pieces are shifting faster than they’d like us to notice. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels lighter, but the ground is still shifting—no one’s sure if it’s settling or giving way. Let’s keep listening, not leaping, and stay ready for whatever comes next."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of trouble are quiet. Still, the old saying holds: even the strongest walls have cracks, and we should keep our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip and more like the quiet before a storm. The usual rhythms are stuttering, and even the most cautious are starting to wonder if the walls are thinner than we thought."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm holding its breath. The usual jokes are sharper, the queues longer, and the elites are quietly rearranging their chairs. Nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are listening."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter these days—like a storm that’s lost its wind. The old rules don’t hold the way they used to, but no one knows yet if the calm will last or if the sky will darken again. Stay ready, but keep your steps quiet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—less tension in the streets, but the quiet isn’t the same as calm. The regime’s moves suggest they’re preparing for something, not just reacting, and that’s worth watching closely."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different now—like the old rules are fading, but no one’s sure what comes next. The usual signs are there, but quieter, as if everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The moment will come when it’s clear who’s still holding the strings—and who’s ready to let go."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s changing—unexpectedly mild for this season, but the old roof is creaking under the weight. Best to keep the doors unlocked, just in case, but don’t rush to open them yet. The wind may shift again before the storm passes."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
